findings.title: OAuth authorization request uses scope, state and code response
findings.detail: The documented authorization request includes client_id, scope, state and response_type=code, and users are redirected to it.
findings.appliesWhen: Customers authorize their individual Todoist accounts

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint

findings.title: data:read grants read-only task access
findings.detail: data:read grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels and filters. It is the scope needed to list active tasks.
findings.appliesWhen: Requested for listing active task titles and paging through results

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks

findings.title: Avoid data:read_write and data:delete for this read-only use case
findings.detail: data:read_write includes write access and data:delete permits deleting data; neither is needed for listing tasks and both conflict with the read-only boundary.
findings.appliesWhen: Only if the app is configured with a broader scope than data:read

evidence.quote: data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
data:delete Grants permission to delete application data, including tasks, labels, and filters.

steps.title: Call GET /api/v1/tasks for the first page
steps.detail: Use the connected test account OAuth access token granted with data:read. Representative input: no request body, sent with an Authorization Bearer header. Expected result: a 200 response with a results array, where each task title is in the content field, plus a next_cursor value. Page and offset parameters are not supported, so later pages must use next_cursor. Boundary check: confirm the token was granted data:read only, send only this GET request, and do not call any write endpoint.
steps.doneWhen: The first response returns 200 with results containing content fields and a next_cursor value for the test account.

evidence.quote: get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks
Note: The page and offset parameters are not supported on this API version.

fields: OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN from the test account token exchange

steps.title: Page through remaining active task results
steps.detail: Use GET /api/v1/tasks with data:read. Start from the page returned by the initial task listing. For each response, read next_cursor and send the same request again with cursor set to that exact value, keeping all other parameters identical. Collect the content of each item in results. Stop only when next_cursor is null, which is the documented end of results. Representative input: NEXT_CURSOR copied from the previous page and an OAuth access token from the connected account. Expected result: a 200 JSON page with results and next_cursor, ending with a null cursor. Boundary check: confirm every request is GET, no task body is sent, and no task is created, updated, completed or deleted.
steps.doneWhen: Pages are fetched until next_cursor is null and all task content values are collected. Boundary check: every request in this step uses GET only and sends no write payload.

steps.title: Fetch following pages with next_cursor until null
steps.detail: Repeat GET /api/v1/tasks, passing the next_cursor value from the previous response as the cursor query parameter, and collect the content of tasks from every page. Representative input: the next_cursor string from the prior page. Expected result: each page adds results until next_cursor is null, which is the documented end of results. Stop only when next_cursor is null, not after a fixed number of pages or an empty page. Boundary check: keep the same read-only GET request and data:read token, and do not call any write endpoint.
steps.doneWhen: The final page returns next_cursor as null and task content from every page has been collected.
